1.explanation: In components/prism-sql.js, the Prism.languages.sql object defines a 'string' token whose pattern only matches single- and double-quoted text: /(^|[^@\\])("|'…)*\2/. Because backticks (`) are omitted from that character class, any text wrapped in backticks doesn’t satisfy the regex and so isn’t highlighted as a string. To fix the bug, you need to expand this regex to include backticks—e.g. replace ("|' ) with ("|'|`)—so that `…` sequences are recognized and styled as strings. The same change will also propagate to the minified version (prism-sql.min.js).
1.bug_scenario: The provided screenshot shows a SQL SELECT statement where table and column names are enclosed in backticks (`), but Prism’s SQL highlighter isn’t treating those backtick-wrapped identifiers as strings—so they remain unstyled. When you wrap identifiers in `…`, they should match the "string" token and receive string highlighting, but the current regex only handles single (') and double (") quotes.

2.explanation: Both the unminified and minified SQL language definitions in Prism define a 'string' pattern that only matches double-quoted (") or single-quoted (') text. It omits the backtick character (`). Since SQL uses backticks to quote identifiers, the regex must include ` as a valid delimiter. By updating the 'string' pattern in both files (components/prism-sql.js and prism-sql.min.js) to include the backtick alongside " and ', the highlighter will correctly recognize and style backtick-quoted segments.
2.bug_scenario: The SQL code uses backtick (`) delimiters around identifiers (e.g. `t`.`col1`, `test_table`) but Prism’s SQL highlighter is not treating text inside `` as a string. In the screenshot the backtick‐quoted segments remain unstyled, whereas quoted strings with " or ' are correctly highlighted. The expected behavior is that content inside backticks should be tokenized as a string.
